units.en: In-game, a support company is a fundamental component of a ⟦0⟧.

Unlike ⟦0⟧, support companies are optional. A division may have up to 5⟦1⟧ support companies, but no more than one of each type. Support companies can alter and improve the stats and fighting capabilities of the division. They generally are cheaper in manpower cost than battalions and do not affect a division's combat width or max speed.
⟦0⟧: Gives a smaller bonus to soft attack than a line regiment's artillery battalion because it has fewer guns. It does not slow the division† or affect paradrops.
⟦0⟧: Gives a smaller bonus to air attack than a line regiment's anti-air battalion because it has fewer guns. It does not slow the division† or affect paradrops.
⟦0⟧: Gives a smaller bonus to hard attack and piercing than a line regiment's anti-tank battalion because it has fewer guns. It does not slow the division† or affect paradrops.
⟦0⟧: Similar to regular support artillery but it also gives a bonus to the division's breakthrough stat, used to avoid enemy attacks when attacking.
⟦0⟧: Increases the Entrenchment stat of the division and helps in attacking forts and river crossings.
⟦0⟧: Increases speed in difficult terrain and the division's Reconnaissance stat, making it easier to counter enemy combat tactics in battle.

⟦0⟧: Gives a bonus to the Suppression stat of its division's line battalions, helping to reduce the effects of partisans. Military Police with 2-6 minimally equipped and trained Cavalry battalions makes an efficient and effective rear-area security division.
⟦0⟧: Adds an equipment reliability bonus to the division, reducing equipment losses from training and combat. Advised for combat units using expensive equipment (like tanks).
⟦0⟧: Increases Trickleback stat (returns percentage of lost manpower to the pool) and reduces experience loss from taking casualties. Advised for front-line combat divisions.
⟦0⟧: Reduces the supply usage of the entire division. This is valuable in areas of low supply and for avoiding the need to disperse for supply reasons.
⟦0⟧: Increases the Initiative stat of the division, speeding up planning and increasing the chance of reinforcement in battle from reserves.

† Note that support companies do not affect a division's speed and do not affect combat width as they are forces that remain behind the fighting front while the "front line" combat battalions engage. Therefore a towed antitank support company does not affect the 12 kph speed of a fast division but adding a towed antitank combat battalion to the regiment lines would slow that same division to the towed anti-tank's base speed of 4 KPH. So support Artillery, Anti-Air or Anti-Tank support units can add valuable capabilities to fast divisions.

An infantry division marching at 4 kph is well-matched by combat battalions marching at 4 kph as well. Additional bonuses and effects of adding a support company to overall division stats can be seen in the tooltip in the division designer. Even though these companies may historically have been much larger than company size, they are referred to as support companies to distinguish them from the battalions in line regiments.
Main article: Division designer § Support companies
In the ⟦0⟧, support companies are represented vertically under the Support section.
Each support company costs ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ to add, replace, or remove from a template.

AA will primarily help protect against tactical bombers and CAS attacking a battle that the division is participating in, allowing multiple divisions in the same battle to pool their AA fire. Towed and self-propelled Anti-Air will only fire at enemy planes attacking that division or other divisions that take part in the same battle.
They do nothing against strategic bombers (they fly too high), so adding AA to garrisons will not help protect industry.

At least as of version 1.3, the Devs have reported⟦0⟧ that attached AA can shoot down fighters, but it takes a lot of it (the example in the video showed multiple line battalions, not just a lone support company). Of course, if you have no fighters, putting AA in every division on the front line may be your only option.

Towed AA units also have half-decent anti-armor capability. For example, the tier 2 towed AA has enough piercing to negate the armor value of tier 1 medium tanks. However, self-propelled AA doesn't have anywhere near as much anti-armor capability. AA does not require tungsten to make, so it may be a budget AT option for minor countries.
Having towed or self-propelled AA in a division reduces the malus that enemy air superiority inflicts.
AA are more efficient than fighters at shooting down planes (version 1.10). AA with 1936 equipment can shoot down up to 5% attack planes per 8 hours.

Engineers provide a movement bonus in forest, jungle, marsh, and rivers. They provide a constant defense bonus in forest, jungle, hills, marsh, rivers, and forts. They also provide an entrenchment bonus on top of that. Upgrading engineers increases the entrenchment bonus and adds additional attack and defense bonuses in forts (II), rivers (III) and urban environments (IV). Lastly, they provide a constant attack bonus to amphibious (naval invasions), which stacks with Marines bonuses. Engineers also increase division defense and soft attack, but not as much as an infantry battalion.

Pioneers are a variant of the engineer support company available to all countries who have unlocked the ⟦0⟧ special forces doctrine. These give less entrenchment, remove their amphibious (naval invasions) attack bonus, do not give terrain bonuses in forest, hills, or jungle terrain, and give worse defense bonuses in marsh, rivers, and forts, but give more breakthrough (especially to marine battalions) and better attack bonuses in marsh, rivers, and forts. They can gain additional bonuses through special forces doctrine upgrades. Crucially, ⟦1⟧ restores some of their jungle terrain defense bonus and also has them provide attack and movement bonuses in jungle terrain, while ⟦2⟧ makes them provide amphibious (naval invasions) attack, defense, and movement bonuses that exceed engineer companies', but only one of these doctrinal bonuses can be active at a time. Pioneers are best used for offensive divisions fighting either across rivers in otherwise flat terrain or in terrain that matches their chosen special forces doctrine bonus. They are otherwise either on par with or inferior to regular engineer companies.

⟦0⟧ introduced the Assault Engineer Company and Armored Engineer Company as a variants of the engineer support company. They are made available after completing the Military Engineering Vehicles special project, though the Armored Engineer Company also requires having completed the 1938 Armored Engineer Company technology. These use armored support vehicle equipment in place of some support equipment and infantry equipment. The equipment differences mean they have increased production cost and add fuel usage to the division, increase its supply use, and reduce its Defense, but they can also provide some additional Armor, Piercing, Soft Attack, Hard Attack, and Breakthrough to the division depending on the equipment variant(s) used. Assault engineers trade most of the engineers' terrain defense and movement bonuses for terrain attack bonuses, and they also provide significant attack and movement bonuses in urban terrain. Instead of providing additional entrenchment to leg infantry battalions, they provide addition breakthrough to those battalions. Armored engineers lose defense bonuses in jungle, marsh, and river terrain compared to regular engineers, but give greater movement bonuses in more terrain types, and provide additional attack bonuses in rivers, forts, and urban terrain as well as in amphibious environments (naval invasions). Armored engineers also provide additional Breakthrough to armor battalions. Tech upgrades to engineers also provide these two support companies with similar bonuses, with assault engineers receiving greater attack bonuses but no defense bonuses and armored engineers receiving greater defense bonuses but no attack bonuses. Due to these differences, assault engineers are best used in offensive divisions, while armored engineers are more niche and best used for defensive divisions that are meant to guard key provinces important enough to justify the increased production costs, especially urban provinces.

A recon company provides a speed bonus on most terrain and a reconnaissance points bonus to the ⟦0⟧ that increases the chance to counter the ⟦1⟧ chosen by the enemy. They also slightly increase division defense and attack. There are different types of recon company with varying abilities and ⟦2⟧: cavalry (1 reconnaissance point), motorized (1.5), armored car (2; requires ⟦3⟧), light tank (1), recon rangers (1; requires ⟦4⟧), or helicopter recon (2; requires ⟦5⟧).

They provide roughly a 10% speed boost on most terrain, varies depending on cavalry, motorized, armored car, or light tank. This speed bonus does not increase with upgrades. Consider the value of increasing the infantry speed from 4 km/h to 4.4 km/h, or motorized/light tanks from 12 km/h to 13.2 km/h, and consider how this may combine with vehicle variants to achieve specific speed targets to outpace or overrun the enemy. The answers will vary from player to player and likely from division to division. For example, exploitation and envelopment divisions may find the extra speed valuable while assault and breakthrough divisions may not, although they may find the combat tactics bonus valuable in intense battles. Additionally, recon companies can help to counter enemy ⟦0⟧, should their tactics have counters available. The side with more reconnaissance points receives a flat bonus equivalent to ⟦1⟧ leader skill points. This is added to the ⟦2⟧'s skill level when determining which side picks their tactics second; the side that picks first has a disadvantage because the other side then knows which available tactics would counter the first side's tactic. It only matters that one side has more points than another, the magnitude of the difference does not matter. Each recon upgrade increases reconnaissance points, and the ⟦3⟧ options ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧ increase reconnaissance points from recon companies as well. Helicopter brigade and motorized military police support companies also increase reconnaissance points and can be used in tandem with any recon company. Factors to consider in evaluating recon companies include the relative range of tactics available to each side, potential importance of counterable tactics to an army's warfighting (e.g., the ⟦6⟧ and ⟦7⟧ tactics can be very useful for tank divisions, but they are countered by the ⟦8⟧ and ⟦9⟧ tactics, respectively), and opposing commander skill levels. When multiple divisions in combat on the same side have multiple, different reconnaissance point values, only the highest value is used for that side.

This support company is not intended for the front lines, or any combat really. It provides a percentage increase to the division's Suppression statistic. Suppression counters partisans operating in a region, preventing them from damaging industry. Best when combined with cavalry, motorized, armored cars, and light tanks, which have better suppression than infantry battalions. While they can simply be added to a garrison division, most prefer to create a division template specifically for MPs.

Motorized Military Police is a variant of military police made available after completing the 1938 technology of the same name that requires having completed the Military Engineering Vehicles special project. It requires military motorcycle equipment in place of some support equipment and infantry equipment. The equipment differences mean it has increased production cost and adds fuel usage to any division it is added to, though this fuel usage is not applied to garrisons that use division templates containing motorized military police. Compared to military police, they have increased supply use, but provide additional Suppression as well as Reconnaissance that stacks with recon companies', and they gain the same benefits with improved technology as regular military police. However, as of 1.15.1, they do not benefit from the large suppression bonus granted by ⟦0⟧ to cavalry battalions, making them potentially give less Suppression to cavalry-heavy garrison templates compared to military police.

Military police or motorized military police can be used as an extra infantry battalion if the need arises, though they give a large hit to organization and it is better to use Support Artillery, Support Rocket Artillery, or Engineers to increase division statistics. While the additional reconnaissance on motorized military police can be useful to eek out a defensive advantage, the fact that divisions with it use fuel when they otherwise wouldn't compounds with the increased production requirements to the point that it can outweight this advantage.

Maintenance companies increase the Reliability statistic of all equipment in a division, thus significantly reducing the amount of equipment lost due to ⟦0⟧. The reliability bonus is shown as a "Reliability Bonus" in the division view, rather than being calculated for each division and then recalculated; as a result, all calculations for this company must be done outside the game.
